patch_description: The current local search only swaps nearby pairs (window of 5, 3 rounds). Scheduling research shows that for sequencing problems, "insertion" moves (remove a transaction and re-insert it at another position) often find improvements that swaps miss, especially when a long transaction should move far back. I propose: (1) add an insertion-move pass to the local search, alternating with the swap pass; (2) widen the swap window slightly; (3) increase restarts so the randomized greedy produces more diverse starting points. Each candidate is evaluated with the actual makespan function `get_opt_seq_cost`, so improvements are guaranteed to be real makespan reductions. This should strictly lower makespan relative to the current swap-only search since every existing move is still available and new improving moves can be accepted.
